description: Focused public-dev pack designed to be harder on proxy routing, bridge-noise rejection, intervention boundaries, and pressure-test design than the main 21-case v14 pack.
notes: These cases are intentionally shaped to better expose skill advantages on causal/proxy/intervention tasks.

cases.title: Homebuilder Miss: Funding Stress Or Demand Softness?
cases.scenario: A morning note combines mortgage data, builder credit signals, order metrics, and website activity after a homebuilder stock selloff.
cases.question: Which proxy family should you prioritize to explain the move, and what evidence would most directly falsify that read?

instantiated_inputs.title: Morning note
instantiated_inputs.content: The stock fell 11% after management guided to lower near-term orders. Analysts noted no major land or permitting update. Channel checks described buyer hesitation around monthly payments rather than reduced tour activity.

instantiated_inputs.title: Market and operating snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: 30-year mortgage rate: +55 bps over 6 weeks. Mortgage applications: -12%. Builder CDS: +38 bps. Website traffic: -1%. Model-home visits: flat. Cancellation rate: +1.2 points. Backlog burn: stable.

options.label: A
options.text: Financing conditions and mortgage affordability are the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: B
options.text: End-demand collapse is the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: C
options.text: Land-supply constraints are the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: D
options.text: Accounting noise is the cleaner proxy family.

cases.title: Alt-Token Slump: Base-Asset Weakness Or Liquidity Drain?
cases.scenario: A crypto market packet compares majors, alt-token liquidity, on-chain activity, and exchange conditions after a sharp decline in a gaming token basket.
cases.question: Which proxy family is the cleaner starting point for the selloff, and what would most directly falsify that interpretation?

instantiated_inputs.title: Crypto desk note
instantiated_inputs.content: BTC and ETH were nearly flat on the day, but gaming and lower-liquidity alt tokens sold off hard. No exploit, governance failure, or delisting notice was reported for the focal token.

instantiated_inputs.title: Cross-market snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: BTC return: +0.3%. ETH return: +0.1%. Alt-token order-book depth: -35%. Perp funding on small tokens: sharply negative. Exchange maintenance on one retail-heavy venue: 2 hours. Game DAU: flat. On-chain fees for the project: flat.

options.label: A
options.text: Base-asset adoption is the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: B
options.text: Retail liquidity and alt-beta risk appetite are the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: C
options.text: A project-specific protocol exploit is the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: D
options.text: Institutional ETF flows are the cleaner proxy family.

cases.title: Airline Selloff: Fuel Shock Or Demand Crack?
cases.scenario: An airline equity drawdown arrives alongside a commodity move, while booking and traffic indicators are updated in the same note.
cases.question: Which proxy family should be treated as the primary causal read, and what would most clearly falsify it?

instantiated_inputs.title: Airline sector note
instantiated_inputs.content: The stock fell after a sharp move in energy markets. Management did not cut capacity or demand commentary, and no labor disruption was disclosed.

instantiated_inputs.title: Operating and market snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: Jet fuel crack spread: +18%. Front-month crude: +11%. Forward bookings: +1%. Load factor guidance: unchanged. Unit revenue guidance: flat. Wage agreement updates: none. FX basket: flat.

options.label: A
options.text: Fuel and input-cost pressure are the primary proxy family.

options.label: B
options.text: End-demand weakness is the primary proxy family.

options.label: C
options.text: Labor disruption is the primary proxy family.

options.label: D
options.text: FX translation is the primary proxy family.

cases.title: Small-Cap Software De-Rate: Duration Pressure Or Product Trouble?
cases.scenario: A software stock sells off with a broader factor move while company-specific operating metrics are also reported.
cases.question: Which proxy family is the cleaner explanation for the move, and what would most directly falsify that read?

instantiated_inputs.title: Software note
instantiated_inputs.content: The company reiterated annual ARR guidance and disclosed no outage, product recall, or major customer loss. The stock fell alongside a broader selloff in long-duration software names.

instantiated_inputs.title: Factor and operating snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: High-yield OAS: +75 bps. 10Y real yield: +19 bps. Small-cap software basket: -11%. ARR guidance: unchanged. Net revenue retention: 112% -> 111%. Churn: flat. Major incident count: 0.

options.label: A
options.text: Financing conditions and discount-rate duration are the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: B
options.text: Product trouble is the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: C
options.text: Channel inventory correction is the cleaner proxy family.

options.label: D
options.text: Accounting restatement risk is the cleaner proxy family.

cases.title: Soybean Rally And Snack-Maker Weakness
cases.scenario: A consumer staples note lists several moving commodities, but only some sit on the company’s true cost path.
cases.question: Which candidate driver is most likely bridge noise rather than the core transmission channel?

instantiated_inputs.title: Staples note
instantiated_inputs.content: The stock traded lower after a basket of agricultural commodities moved higher. Management commentary emphasizes freight, packaging resin, palm oil, and cocoa as the main variable costs.

instantiated_inputs.title: Cost exposure snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: Soybeans: +9%. Palm oil: +4%. Cocoa: +6%. Packaging resin: +7%. Freight surcharge impact: +110 bps to COGS. Soy exposure in the focal brand mix: not material.

options.label: A
options.text: The soybean rally is most likely bridge noise rather than the core driver.

options.label: B
options.text: Freight surcharges are most likely bridge noise rather than the core driver.

options.label: C
options.text: Packaging-resin inflation is most likely bridge noise rather than the core driver.

options.label: D
options.text: Palm-oil and cocoa costs are most likely bridge noise rather than the core driver.

cases.title: Regional Bank Stress And A Small-Cap SaaS Selloff
cases.scenario: A software stock trades off during regional-bank stress even though the company has no direct deposit or lending disclosure in the packet.
cases.question: Which transmission path is the most supportable causal explanation?

instantiated_inputs.title: Market note
instantiated_inputs.content: The company stated that cash is spread across money-center banks and disclosed no unusual financing event. The stock still sold off with other long-duration software names when regional banks weakened.

instantiated_inputs.title: Factor snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: Regional bank ETF: -14%. Small-cap software basket: -9%. HY OAS: +48 bps. Company net cash: positive. Revenue guidance: unchanged.

options.label: A
options.text: No plausible path exists from regional-bank stress to the software stock.

options.label: B
options.text: Direct deposit-loss exposure is the most supportable path.

options.label: C
options.text: A valuation-duration and refinancing channel is the most supportable path.

options.label: D
options.text: A hardware inventory channel is the most supportable path.

cases.title: Rare-Earth Spike Into EV Gross Margin
cases.scenario: A commodity shock looks intuitively relevant, but the evidence packet includes cost-share and contracting details that constrain near-term transmission.
cases.question: How strong is the near-term transmission from rare-earth prices to the EV maker’s gross margin?

instantiated_inputs.title: Supply-chain note
instantiated_inputs.content: Rare-earth spot prices jumped after export restrictions. The automaker’s procurement note says the focal materials are covered by fixed contracts for the next two quarters.

instantiated_inputs.title: Cost-structure snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: Rare-earth component share of COGS: 1.2%. Fixed-price coverage horizon: 2 quarters. Battery metals and logistics remain the larger variable exposures.

options.label: A
options.text: It is a strong and immediate primary driver of gross margin.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a moderate near-term driver, but not the dominant one.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a weak, bridge-heavy near-term channel rather than a clean primary driver.

options.label: D
options.text: No judgment of any kind is possible from the packet.

cases.title: Biotech Rally: Primary Driver Or Pure Squeeze?
cases.scenario: A market-news packet contains a regulatory catalyst, a later rumor, and evidence that short interest may have amplified the move.
cases.question: Which explanation best fits the move without overstating the evidence?

instantiated_inputs.title: Event timeline
instantiated_inputs.content: 09:00: FDA advisory panel votes favorably on the therapy. 09:05: stock opens sharply higher. 12:10: an unconfirmed social-media rumor mentions a possible acquisition. Short interest entering the day was 24% of float.

instantiated_inputs.title: Intraday move summary
instantiated_inputs.content: Open-to-10am move: +21%. Noon-to-close incremental move: +6%. Borrow fee: elevated. Company filings: no acquisition filing or comment.

options.label: A
options.text: The unconfirmed acquisition rumor is the primary driver.

options.label: B
options.text: Short-squeeze dynamics are the primary driver, with no stronger causal event in the packet.

options.label: C
options.text: The FDA advisory-panel vote is the primary driver, while squeeze dynamics likely amplified the move.

options.label: D
options.text: No supportable causal read is possible from the packet.

cases.title: Price Cut And Sales-Comp Rewrite In The Same Week
cases.scenario: Leadership wants the effect of a price cut on unit sales, but the operating packet shows another major commercial intervention at the same time and in the same weak regions.
cases.question: Is the causal effect of the price cut on units identified from the observed packet?

instantiated_inputs.title: Commercial rollout note
instantiated_inputs.content: The company reduced list price by 8% in the weakest four regions and simultaneously changed sales compensation to reward unit volume instead of gross profit dollars.

instantiated_inputs.title: Observed outcome summary
instantiated_inputs.content: The treated regions saw unit growth accelerate after the rollout. Untreated regions kept the old price and old comp plan. No randomization or staggered timing was used.

options.label: A
options.text: Yes. A simple before/after comparison identifies the price effect.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes. Region controls are enough to identify the price effect.

options.label: C
options.text: No. The packet bundles two interventions on selected weak regions.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes. A treated-vs-untreated snapshot identifies the price effect.

cases.title: Predictive Maintenance Rolled Out To The Worst Plants First
cases.scenario: A maintenance model was adopted first where failures were already highest, and leadership wants a credible evaluation design.
cases.question: Which design is most defensible for estimating the model’s effect, and what is the main threat to validity?

instantiated_inputs.title: Rollout summary
instantiated_inputs.content: The predictive-maintenance model was launched first at plants with the highest prior failure rates. Failure rates fell after deployment, but the untreated plants were lower-risk to begin with.

instantiated_inputs.title: Plant summary
instantiated_inputs.content: Four treated plants adopted in month 1, four control plants remained on the old process. Treated plants started with materially worse pre-period failure levels.

options.label: A
options.text: A simple before/after comparison is the most defensible design.

options.label: B
options.text: A matched or staggered difference-in-differences event study with pretrend checks is the most defensible design.

options.label: C
options.text: A post-only treated-vs-control cross-section is the most defensible design.

options.label: D
options.text: Instrumenting treatment with plant size is the most defensible design.

cases.title: Credit-Limit Increases For Prequalified Users
cases.scenario: A consumer-finance team increased credit limits only for users already scored as especially attractive, then asked for the treatment effect on purchase frequency.
cases.question: Can the treated-vs-untreated mean difference identify the effect on purchase frequency?

instantiated_inputs.title: Risk-team note
instantiated_inputs.content: Only prequalified users with high internal scores received the limit increase. The untreated pool contains more low-score and lower-spend customers.

instantiated_inputs.title: Outcome summary
instantiated_inputs.content: Treated users increased purchase frequency after the offer. Current observables include age bucket, region, and merchant mix, but not latent spending appetite or the full internal scorecard.

options.label: A
options.text: Yes. The treated-vs-untreated mean difference identifies the treatment effect.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes. The current covariates are enough to remove the bias.

options.label: C
options.text: No. Selection on latent spending propensity still blocks identification.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes. Stable merchant mix is sufficient to identify the effect.

cases.title: Warehouse Expedite Policy And Temporary Staffing
cases.scenario: An operations packet shows late shipments falling after a new expedite policy, but staffing changed in the same window.
cases.question: Is the expedite-policy effect identified from the observed packet, and what is the most important confound?

instantiated_inputs.title: Operations note
instantiated_inputs.content: A warehouse introduced a new expedite policy during peak season. The same week, temporary staffing was increased by 18% and overtime rules were relaxed.

instantiated_inputs.title: Late-shipment summary
instantiated_inputs.content: Late shipments fell from 9.4% to 6.7% after the policy week. No site-level stagger or holdout group is available in the packet.

options.label: A
options.text: Yes. Staffing is too small to matter here.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes. Controlling for shift is enough to identify the policy effect.

options.label: C
options.text: No. The simultaneous temporary-staffing change is the key confound.

options.label: D
options.text: No. The outcome metric itself is unusable.

cases.title: Which First Pressure Test Separates Financing Stress From Demand Softness?
cases.scenario: A distributor note leaves two live stories on the table, and the task is to pick the first stress lever that would most efficiently separate them.
cases.question: Which first pressure test would best separate financing stress from demand softness?

instantiated_inputs.title: Agent brief
instantiated_inputs.content: Rate-sensitive customer verticals have slowed, but service attach and installed-base usage remain stable. Credit spreads widened and management said quote activity was healthy but close timing stretched.

instantiated_inputs.title: Commercial snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: New orders: -4%. Cancellations: +2 points. Service attach: flat. Installed-base usage: flat. HY OAS: +62 bps. Accounts receivable days: +4 days.

options.label: A
options.text: Stress commodity input costs and inspect gross margin.

options.label: B
options.text: Stress financing conditions and inspect orders plus cancellations.

options.label: C
options.text: Stress FX and inspect backlog conversion.

options.label: D
options.text: Stress labor availability and inspect headcount growth.

cases.title: Fuel Shock Or Demand Weakness: Which Probe Comes First?
cases.scenario: An airline packet leaves cost shock and demand weakness as competing stories, and the task is to choose the first clean pressure test.
cases.question: Which first pressure test most cleanly distinguishes fuel shock from demand weakness?

instantiated_inputs.title: Agent brief
instantiated_inputs.content: The stock sold off with energy markets. Forward bookings and capacity plans held steady. Analysts want the first probe that would most quickly separate cost pressure from true demand deterioration.

instantiated_inputs.title: Sector snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: Jet fuel crack: +18%. Forward bookings: +1%. Load factor guidance: unchanged. Unit revenue: flat. FX: flat.

options.label: A
options.text: Stress jet-fuel costs and inspect unit margin or EPS sensitivity.

options.label: B
options.text: Stress load factor and inspect fuel hedges.

options.label: C
options.text: Stress FX and inspect baggage-fee revenue.

options.label: D
options.text: Stress wage inflation and inspect loyalty signups.

cases.title: EV Supplier Drop: Lithium Pass-Through Or Customer Inventory Reset?
cases.scenario: A supplier stock weakens while both upstream commodity and downstream customer signals are moving, and the analyst must pick the first separating probe.
cases.question: Which first pressure test best distinguishes lithium pass-through from customer inventory reset?

instantiated_inputs.title: Agent brief
instantiated_inputs.content: Lithium prices softened, but customer inventory days also rose across two major OEMs. The supplier guides to softer near-term shipments without changing long-run content assumptions.

instantiated_inputs.title: Supplier snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: Lithium spot: -14%. Customer inventory days: +11 days. OEM production schedules: trimmed for next quarter. Supplier gross-margin guide: only modestly lower. Backlog conversion: slowing.

options.label: A
options.text: Stress lithium prices and inspect next-quarter gross margin.

options.label: B
options.text: Stress customer inventory and build schedules, then inspect shipments and backlog conversion.

options.label: C
options.text: Stress FX and inspect operating expenses.

options.label: D
options.text: Stress energy prices and inspect depreciation.

cases.title: Residential Solar Miss: Policy Step-Down Or Sales Execution?
cases.scenario: The packet leaves policy and execution stories both live, and the evaluation asks for the cleanest first probe to challenge the leading thesis.
cases.question: Which pressure test most directly challenges the thesis that policy incentive step-down is the main driver?

instantiated_inputs.title: Agent brief
instantiated_inputs.content: Order volume weakened after a state incentive step-down, but channel checks also mention elevated rep turnover and slower lead follow-up times.

instantiated_inputs.title: Sales funnel snapshot
instantiated_inputs.content: Lead volume: -3%. Lead-to-booking conversion: -16%. Incentive value: -22%. Sales-rep turnover: +8 points. Follow-up time: slower by 1.4 days.

options.label: A
options.text: Stress incentive-policy generosity and inspect lead-to-booking conversion.

options.label: B
options.text: Stress panel input costs and inspect gross margin.

options.label: C
options.text: Stress installer hiring and inspect warehouse rent.

options.label: D
options.text: Stress bitcoin and inspect lead generation.
